marrow__BIOCHEM_CH26_Q016.original:
Self-splicing introns do not require a spliceosome or any other proteins for the splicing reaction.
Self-splicing introns fold into complex loops and undergo transesterification reactions, thus
undergoing self splicing.
Other options:
Option A: Split genes have the advantage that they allow alternative splicing so that a single gene
can code for variant forms of the same protein.
Option C: B-thalassemia results from the faulty splicing of the B-globin transcript. However, the
spliceosome is normal and the reason for the fault is a mutation in the B-globin gene itself.
Option D: Splicing occurs in the nucleus and mature transcripts are then transported into the
cytosol for translation (protein synthesis) to occur.
